newsitem.title: UK: E.Europe beet crop seen on course despite rains.
newsitem.headline: E.Europe beet crop seen on course despite rains.

text.p: Forecasts of a slightly drier trend in key sugar beet growing areas of eastern Europe should keep crop prospects near average after the recent torrential rains, F.O. Licht said on Wednesday.
"Beet crop potential is stable and the weather outlook for a slightly drier trend should keep prospects near average," Licht said in its daily report.

It was referring to Poland, Slovakia and the Czech Republic, where heavy rainfall has now eased. Rains also eased in the beet areas of the former Soviet Union during the week ended July 29, Licht said.

But precipitation amounting to between 180 and 300 percent of normal levels in Ukraine could have a slightly negative crop impact, although drier weather expected in the first half of August could improve potential.
Near normal rainfall in July in western Russia and in the western Volga valley could raise yields above average, it added.
In western Europe, beet areas turned drier during the week under review.
Licht cited industry sources in northern Germany saying beet yields should be higher than last year due to favourable weather.
Crop conditions were stable in Spain although soil moisture was declining in the north, it said.
